verses.sanskrit:
शौनक उवाच।
              कथं स भगवान्देवो यज्ञेष्वग्रहरः प्रभुः। यज्ञधारी च सततं वेदवेदाङ्गवित्तथा॥१॥
verses.english: Saunaka said is that illustrious god, viz., the powerful Narayana, who is a master of the Vedas and their branches, at once the doer and the enjoyer of sacrifices?

verses.sanskrit: निवृत्तं चास्थितो धर्मं क्षमी भागवतः प्रभुः। निवृत्तिधर्मान्विदधे स एव भगवान्प्रभुः॥२॥
verses.english: Endued with forgiveness, he has adopted, again, the Religion of Renunciation. Indeed, it is that holy and powerful one who has himself laid down the duties of Renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: कथं प्रवृत्तिधर्मेषु भागार्हा देवताः कृताः। कथं निवृत्तिधर्माश्च कृता व्यावृत्तबुद्धयः॥३॥
verses.english: Why then has he made many of the gods the takers of shares in sacrifices which, of course, are all due to the Religion of Action. Why has he again created some with an opposite disposition, for they follow the ordinances of the Religion of Renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: एतं नः संशयं सौते छिन्धि गुह्यं सनातनम्। त्वया नारायणकथाः श्रुता वै धर्मसंहिताः॥४॥
verses.english: Do you, O Suta, remove this doubt of ours. This doubt seems to be eternal and is filled with great mystery. You have heard all discourses on Narayana, which are consistent with the (other) scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: सौतिरुवाच । जनमेजयेन यत्पृष्टः शिष्यो व्यासस्य धीमतः। तत्तेऽहं कथयिष्यामि पौराणं शौनकोत्तम॥५॥
verses.english: O excellent Saunaka, I shall recount to you what Vaishampayana, the disciple of the intelligent Vyasa, said when questioned on these very topics by king Janamejaya.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा माहात्म्यमेतस्य देहिनां परमात्मनः। जनमेजयो महाप्राज्ञो वैशम्पायनमब्रवीत्॥६॥
verses.english: Having heard the discourse on the glory of Narayana who is the Soul of all embodied creatues, Janamejaya, gifted with great intelligence and wisdom, asked Vaishampayana about these very topics.

verses.sanskrit:
जनमेजय उवाच।
              इमे सब्रह्मका लोकाः ससुरासुरमानवाः। क्रियास्वभ्युदयोक्तासु सक्ता दृश्यन्ति सर्वशः॥७॥
verses.english: The whole world of Being, with Brahman, the gods, the Asuras, and human beings are seen to be deeply attached to acts which yield prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: मोक्षश्चोक्तस्त्वया ब्रह्मन्निर्वाणं परमं सुखम्। ये तु मुक्ता भवन्तीह पुण्यपापविवर्जिताः॥८॥
verses.english: Liberation has, O twice-born one, been described by you to be the highest happiness and to consist of the cessation of existence. They who being shorn of both merit and demerit, become liberated, succeed, we hear, in entering the great God of a thousand rays.

verses.sanskrit: ते सहस्रार्चिषं देवं प्रविशन्तीह शुश्रुम। अयं हि दुरनुष्ठेयो मोक्षधर्मः सनातनः॥९॥
verses.english: It seems to be, O Brahmana, that the eternal religion of Liberation is highly difficult of observance. Turning away from it, all the gods have become enjoyers of the libations of clarified butter poured with Mantras on sacrificial fires and other offerings presented to them by similar means.

verses.sanskrit: यं हित्वा देवताः सर्वा हव्यकव्यभुजोऽभवन्। किं च ब्रह्मा च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्च बलभित्प्रभुः॥१०॥
सूर्यस्ताराधिपो वायुरग्निर्वरुण एव च। आकाशं जगती चैव ये च शेषा दिवौकसः॥११॥
verses.english: Then, again, Brahman, and Rudra, the powerful Sakra the killer of Vala, the Sun, the Lord of the stars, the Wind-god, the god of fire, the god of the Waters, Infinite Space, the Universe too and the rest of the dwellers of heaven,-these, it seems do not know the way of securing an annihilation of conscious existence that is encompassed by one's own efforts.

verses.sanskrit: प्रलयं न विजानन्ति आत्मनः परिनिर्मितम्। ततस्तेनास्थिता मार्गं ध्रुवमक्षरमव्ययम्॥१२॥
स्मृतिकालपरीमाणं प्रवृत्तिं ये समास्थिताः। दोषः कालपरीमाणे महानेष क्रियावताम्॥१३॥
verses.english: Hence, perhaps, they have not followed the path which is certain, indestructible, and immutable. Hence, perhaps turning away from that path, they have adopted the Religion of Action which leads to conscious existence that is measured by time.

verses.sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं विप्र हृदि शल्यमिवार्पितम्। छिन्धीतिहासकथनात्परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥१४॥
verses.english: This, indeed, is one great defeat of those who are wedded to acts, for all their rewards are for the time being. This doubt, O twiceborn one, exists in my heart like a dagger! Tear it out by recounting to me some discourses of old on this subject. Great is my curiosity to listen to you.

verses.sanskrit: कथं भागहराः प्रोक्ता देवताः क्रतुषु द्विज। किमर्थं चाध्वरे ब्रह्मन्निज्यन्ते त्रिदिवौकसः॥१५॥
verses.english: Why, O twice-born one, have the gods been said to be takers of their respective shares of sacrificial offerings presented to them with the help of Mantras in sacrifices of various kinds? Why, again, are the dwellers of heaven worshipped in sacrifices?

verses.sanskrit: ये च भागं प्रगृह्णन्ति यज्ञेषु द्विजसत्तम। ये यजन्तो महायज्ञैः कस्य भागं ददन्ति वै॥१६॥
verses.english: And, O best of twice-born ones to whom do they, who partake of offerings in sacrifices performed to their honour, themselves make offerings when they perform great sacrifices?

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              अहो गूढतमः प्रश्नस्त्वया पृष्टो जनेश्वर। नातप्ततपसा ह्येष नावेदविदुषा तथा॥१७॥
verses.english: The question you have put to me, O king, relates to a deed mystery. No man can quickly answer it who has not practised penances, and who is not acquainted with the Puranas.

verses.sanskrit: नापुराणविदा चैव शक्यो व्याहर्तुमञ्जसा। हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि यन्मे पृष्टः पुरा गुरुः॥१८॥
कृष्णद्वैपायनो व्यासो वेदव्यासो महानृषिः। सुमन्तुर्जैमिनिश्चैव पैलश्च सुदृढव्रतः॥१९॥
verses.english: I shall, however, answer you by reciting to you what my preceptor the Island-born Krishna, otherwise called Vyasa, the great Rishi who has divided the Vedas, had said to us on a former occasion when questioned by us.

verses.sanskrit: अहं चतुर्थः शिष्यो वै पञ्चमश्च शुकः स्मृतः। एतान्समागतान्सर्वान्पञ्च शिष्यान्दमान्वितान्॥२०॥
verses.english: Sumanta, and Jaimini, and Paila of firm vows, and myself as the fourth, and Shuka. as the fifth, were disciples of the illustrious Vyasa.

verses.sanskrit: शौचाचारसमायुक्ताञ्जिक्रोधान् जितेन्द्रियान्। वेदानध्यापयामास महाभारतपञ्चमान्॥२१॥
verses.english: We, five in all, endued with self-control and purity of observances, had completely mastered anger and controlled our senses. Our preceptor used to teach us the Vedas having the Mahabharata for their fifth.

verses.sanskrit: मेरौ गिरिवरे रम्ये सिद्धचारणसेविते। तेषामभ्यस्यतां वेदान् कदाचित्संशयोऽभवत्॥२२॥
verses.english: Once on a time, on the breast of that foremost of mountains, viz., the delightful Meru, inhabited by Siddhas and Charanas while we were engaged in reading the Vedas, this very doubt sprang in our minds, that has been given vent to by you to-day. We, therefore, asked our preceptor about it. It heared the answer that our preceptor made. I shall now recount that answer to you, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: एष वै यस्त्वया पृष्टस्तेन तेषां प्रकीर्तितः। ततः श्रुतो मया चापि तवाख्येयोऽद्य भारत॥२३॥
शिष्याणां वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वाज्ञानतमोनुदः। पराशरसुतः श्रीमान्व्यासो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत्॥२४॥
मया हि सुमहत्तप्तं तपः परमदारुणम् । भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च जानीयामिति सत्तमाः॥२५॥
तस्य मे तप्ततपसो निगृहीतेन्द्रियस्य च। नारायणप्रसादेन क्षीरोदस्यानुकूलतः॥२६॥
त्रैकालिकमिदं ज्ञानं प्रादुर्भूतं यथेप्सितम्। तच्छृणुध्वं यथान्यायं वक्ष्ये संशयमुत्तमम्॥२७॥
यथा वृत्तं हि कल्पादौ दृष्टं मे ज्ञानचक्षुषा। परमात्मेति यं प्राहुः सांख्ययोगविदो जनाः॥२८॥
महापुरुषसंज्ञां स लभते स्वेन कर्मणा। तस्मात्प्रसूतमव्यक्तं प्रधानं तं विदुर्बुधाः॥२९॥
अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तमुत्पन्नं लोकसृष्ट्यर्थमीश्वरात्। अनिरुद्धो हि लोकेषु महानात्मेति कथ्यते॥३०॥
योऽसौ व्यक्तत्वमापन्नो निर्ममे च पितामहम्। सोऽहंकार इति प्रोक्तः सर्वतेजोमयो हि सः॥३१॥
पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्। अहंकारप्रसूतानि महाभूतानि पञ्चधा॥३२॥
महाभूतानि सृष्ट्वैव तान्गुणान्निर्ममे पुनः। भूतेभ्यश्चैव निष्पन्ना मूर्तिमन्तश्च तान् शृणु॥३३॥
मरीचिरङ्गिराश्चात्रिः पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः। वसिष्ठश्च महात्मा वै मनुः स्वायंभुवस्तथा॥३४॥
ज्ञेयाः प्रकृतयोऽष्टौ ता यासु लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः। वेदवेदाङ्गसंयुक्तान्यज्ञान्यज्ञाङ्गसंयुतान्॥३५॥
निर्ममे लोकसिद्ध्यर्थं ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः। अष्टाभ्यः प्रकृतिभ्यश्च जातं विश्वमिदं जगत्॥३६॥
रुद्रो रोषात्मको जातो दशान्यान्सोऽसृजत् स्वयम्। एकादशैते रुद्रास्तु विकारपुरुषाः स्मृताः॥३७॥
ते रुद्राः प्रकृतिश्चैव सर्वे चैव सुरर्षयः। उत्पन्ना लोकसिद्ध्यर्थं ब्रह्माणं समुपस्थिताः॥३८॥
वयं सृष्टा हि भगवंस्त्वया च प्रभविष्णुना। येन यस्मिन्नधीकारे वर्तितव्यं पितामह॥३९॥
योऽसौ त्वयाभिनिर्दिष्टो ह्यधिकारोऽर्थचिन्तकः। परिपाल्यः कथं तेन साहंकारेण कर्तृणा॥४०॥
प्रदिशस्व बलं तस्य योऽधिकारार्थचिन्तकः। एवमुक्तो महादेवो देवांस्तानिदमब्रवीत्॥४१॥

ब्रह्मोवाच।
              साध्वहं ज्ञापितो देवा युष्माभिर्भद्रमस्तु वः। ममाप्येषा समुत्पन्ना चिन्ता या भवतां मता॥४२॥
लोकत्रयस्य कृत्स्नस्य कथं कार्यः परिग्रहः। कथं बलक्षयो न स्याद्युष्माकं ह्यात्मनश्च मे॥४३॥
इतः सर्वेऽपि गच्छामः शरणं लोकसाक्षिणम्। महापुरुषमव्यक्तं स नो वक्ष्यति यद्धितम्॥४४॥
ततस्ते ब्रह्मणा सार्धमृषयो विबुधास्तथा। क्षीरोदस्योत्तरं कूलं जग्मुर्लोकहितार्थिनः॥४५॥
ते तपः समुपातिष्ठन्ब्रह्मोक्तं वेदकल्पितम्। स महानियमो नाम तपश्चर्यासु दारुणः॥४६॥
ऊर्ध्वा दृष्टिर्बाहवश्च एकाग्रं च मनोऽभवत्। एकपादाः स्थिताः सर्वे काष्ठभूताः समाहिताः॥४७॥
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं ते तपस्तप्त्वा सुदारुणम्। शुश्रुवुर्मधुरां वाणीं वेदवेदाङ्गभूषिताम्॥४८॥
श्रीभगवानुवाच । भो भोः सब्रह्मका देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः। स्वागतेनार्च्य वः सर्वान् श्रावये वाक्यमुत्तमम्॥४९॥
विज्ञातं वो मया कार्यं तच्च लोकहितं महत्। प्रवृत्तियुक्तं कर्तव्यं युष्मत्प्राणोपबृंहणम्॥५०॥
सुतप्तं च तपो देवा ममाराधनकाम्यया। भोक्ष्यथास्य महासत्त्वास्तपसः फलमुत्तमम्॥५१॥
एष ब्रह्मा लोकगुरुर्महान् लोकपितामहः। यूयं च विबुधश्रेष्ठा मां यजध्वं समाहिताः॥५२॥
सर्वे भागान्कल्पयध्वं यज्ञेषु मम नित्यशः। तथा श्रेयोऽभिधास्यामि यथाधीकारमीश्वराः॥५३॥

वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              श्रुत्वैतद्देवदेवस्य वाक्यं हृष्टतनूरुहाः। ततस्ते विबुधाः सर्वे ब्रह्मा च महर्षयः॥५४॥
वेददृष्टेन विधिना वैष्णवं क्रतुमाहरन्। तस्मिन्सत्रे सदा ब्रह्मा स्वयं भागमकल्पयत्॥५५॥
verses.english: They immediately made arrangements for a sacrifice in honour of Vishnu according to the Vedic ordinances. In that sacrifice, Brahman himself assigned a portion of the offerings to Vishnu.

verses.sanskrit: देवा देवर्षयश्चैव स्वं स्वं भागमकल्पयन्। ते कार्तयुगधर्माणो भागाः परमसत्कृताः॥५६॥
verses.english: Similarly the gods and the celestial Rishis also, dedicated similar portions each to the great God. The portions, thus offered with great respect to Vishnu, were about both the quantity and the quality of the articles used, according to the ordinances laid down for the Krita age.

verses.sanskrit: प्राहुरादित्यवर्णं तं पुरुषं तमसः परम्। बृहन्तं सर्वगं देवमीशानं वरदं प्रभुम्॥५७॥
verses.english: The gods and the Rishis and Brahman, in that sacrifice, worshipped the great God as one having the complexion of the Sun, as the foremost of Beings, situate beyond the reach of Ignorance, vast, pervading all things, the Supreme Lord of all, the giver of boons, and endued with power.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽथ वरदो देवस्तान्सर्वानमरान्स्थितान्। अशरीरो बभाषेदं वाक्यं खस्थो महेश्वरः॥५८॥
verses.english: Thus worshipped by them the boon-giving and great God, invisible and bodiless, addressed those assembled celestials from heaven and said to them

verses.sanskrit: येन यः कल्पितो भागः स तथा मामुपागतः। प्रीतोऽहं प्रदिशाम्यद्य फलमावृत्तिलक्षणम्॥५९॥
verses.english: I have received the offerings dedicated by you in this sacrifice. I am pleased with all of you. I shall confer rewards on you that will, however, be fraught with ends from where there will be return.

verses.sanskrit: एतद्वो लक्षणं देवा मत्प्रसादसमुद्भवम्। स्वयं यज्ञैर्यजमानाः समाप्तवरदक्षिणैः॥६०॥
verses.english: This shall be your distinctive characteristic, ye gods, from this day, on account of my favours and kindness for you. Celebrating sacrifices in every cycle, with large presents, you will become enjoyers of fruits born of Action.

verses.sanskrit: युगे युगे भविष्यध्वं प्रवृत्तिफलभागिनः। यज्ञैर्ये चापि यक्ष्यन्ति सर्वलोकेषु वै सुराः॥६१॥
verses.english: You gods, those men also that will celebrate sacrifices, according to the Vedic ordinances, will give to all of you, shares of their sacrificial offerings.

verses.sanskrit: कल्पयिष्यन्ति वो भागांस्ते नरा वेदकल्पितान्। यो मे यथा कल्पितवान्भागमस्मिन्महाक्रतौ॥६२॥
स तथा यज्ञभागार्हो वेदसूत्रे मया कृतः। यूयं लोकान्भावयध्वं यज्ञभागफलोचिताः॥६३॥
verses.english: In the Veda-sutras I make him the receiver of a share like that which he has himself offered one in this sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वार्थचिन्तका लोके यथाधीकारनिर्मिताः। याः क्रियाः प्रचरिष्यन्ति प्रवृत्तिफलसत्कृताः॥६४॥
verses.english: Created to superintend the affairs of your respective jurisdictions, do you uphold the worlds according to your strength as dependent on the shares you receive in those sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: आभिराप्यायितबला लोकान्वै धारयिष्यथ । यूयं हि भाविता यज्ञैः सर्वयज्ञेषु मानवैः॥६५॥
verses.english: Indeed, receiving strength from those rites and observances that will be in vogue in the several worlds, originating from the fruits of action, do ye continue to uphold the affairs of those worlds.

verses.sanskrit: मां ततो भावयिष्यध्वमेषा वो भावना मम। इत्यर्थं निर्मिता वेदा यज्ञाश्चौषधिभिः सह॥६६॥
verses.english: Strengthened by the sacrifices that will be celebrated by men, ye will strengthen me. These are the thoughts that I cherish for you

verses.sanskrit: एभिः सम्यक्प्रयुक्तैर्हि प्रीयन्ते देवताः क्षितौ। निर्माणमेतद्युष्माकं प्रवृत्तिगुणकल्पितम्॥६७॥
verses.english: It is for this that I have created the Vedas and sacrifices and plants and herbs. Duly served with these by human beings on Earth, the gods will be pleased.

verses.sanskrit: मया कृतं सुरश्रेष्ठा यावत्कल्पक्षयादिह। चिन्तयध्वं लोकहितं यथाधीकारमीश्वराः॥६८॥
verses.english: You foremost of gods, till the end of this aeon, I have ordained your creation, making your constitutions depend upon the result of the religion of Action. You foremost of Beings, do you then, about your respective jurisdictions, engage yourselves in seeking the welfare of the three worlds.

verses.sanskrit: मरीचिरंगिराश्चात्रिः पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः। वसिष्ठ इति सप्तैते मानसा निर्मिता हि ते॥६९॥
verses.english: Marichi, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasistha,-these seven Rishis have been created by the fiat of the will.

verses.sanskrit: एते वेदविदो मुख्या वेदाचार्याश्च कल्पिताः। प्रवृत्तिधर्मिणश्चैव प्राजापत्ये च कल्पिताः॥७०॥
verses.english: These will become the foremost of all persons versed in the Vedas. In fact, they will become the preceptors of the Vedas. They will follow the Religion of Action, for they have been intended to devote themselves to the act of procreating children.

verses.sanskrit: अयं क्रियावतां पन्था व्यक्तीभूतः सनातनः। अनिरुद्ध इति प्रोक्तो लोकसर्गकरः प्रभुः॥७१॥
सनः सनत्सुजातश्च सनकः ससनन्दनः। सनत्कुमारः कपिल: सप्तमश्च सनातनः॥७२॥
verses.english: Sana, Sanatsujata, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumara, Kapila, and Sanatana,—these seven Rishis are known as the spiritual sons of Brahman. Their knowledge comes to them of itself. These seven follow the Religion of Renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: सप्तैते मानसाः प्रोक्ता ऋषयो ब्रह्मणः सुताः। स्वयमागतविज्ञाना निवृत्तिं धर्ममास्थिताः॥७३॥
एते योगविदो मुख्या: सांख्यज्ञानविशारदाः। आचार्या धर्मशास्त्रेषु मोक्षधर्मप्रवर्तकाः॥७४॥
verses.english: They are the foremost of all persons conversant with Yoga. They have a profound knowledge of the Sankhya philosophy. They are teachers of the scriptures on duty and it is they who introduce the duties of the Religion of Renunciation and cause them flow in the worlds.

verses.sanskrit: यतोऽहं प्रसृतः पूर्वमव्यक्तात्त्रिगुणो महान्। तस्मात्परतरो योऽसौ क्षेत्रज्ञ इति कल्पितः॥७५॥
verses.english: From Nature has sprung Consciousness and the three great qualities. Transcending Nature is called Soul.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽहं क्रियावतां पन्थाः पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभः। यो यथा निर्मितो जन्तुर्यस्मिन्यस्मिंश्च कर्मणि॥७६॥
verses.english: That Soul is myself. The path of those who follow acts is fraught with return. One cannot, by that path, reach the place whence there is no return. Different creatures have been created with different objects. Some are intended for the Path of Action and some for that of Renunciation. One enjoys the the reward, according to the path that he follows. This Brahman is the lord of all the worlds. Endued with power, it is he who creates the universe.

verses.sanskrit: प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा तत्फलं सोऽश्नुते महत्। एष लोकगुरुर्ब्रह्मा जगदादिकरः प्रभुः॥७७॥
एष माता पिता चैव युष्माकं च पितामहः। मयाऽनुशिष्टो भविता सर्वभूतवरप्रदः॥७८॥
verses.english: He is your mother and father, and he is your grandfather. At my behest, he will grant boons to all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: अस्य चैवात्मजो रुद्रो ललाटाद्यः समुत्थितः। ब्रह्मानुशिष्टो भविता सर्वभूतधरः प्रभुः॥७९॥
verses.english: His son Rudra, who has originated from his brow at his behest, will, gifted with power, uphold all created beings.

verses.sanskrit: गच्छध्वं स्वानधीकारांश्चिन्तयध्वं यथाविधि। प्रवर्तन्तां क्रियाः सर्वाः सर्वलोकेषु मा चिरम्॥८०॥
verses.english: Go you to your respective jurisdictions, and seek, according to the ordinances, the welfare of the world! Let all the scriptural acts flow in all the worlds. Let there be no delay in this.

verses.sanskrit: प्रदिश्यन्तां च कर्माणि प्राणिनां गतयस्तथा। परिनिष्ठितकालानि आयूंषीह सुरोत्तमाः॥८१॥
verses.english: You foremost of gods, do ye ordain the acts of all creatures and the ends that they are come by. Do ye also set the limits of the lives of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: इदं कृतयुगं नाम कालः श्रेष्ठः प्रवर्तितः। अहिंस्या यज्ञपशवो युगेऽस्मिन्न तदन्यथा॥८२॥
verses.english: This present cycle that is going on is the foremost of all epochs and should be known by the name of Krita. In this cycle living creatures should not be celebrated. It should be as I ordain and let it not be otherwise.

verses.sanskrit: चतुष्पात्सकलो धर्मो भविष्यत्यत्र वै सुराः। ततस्त्रेतायुगं नाम त्रयी यत्र भविष्यति॥८३॥
verses.english: In this age, ye celestials, virtue will flourish in full. After this age will come the cycle called Treta. The Vedas, in that cycle, will lose one quarter. Only three of them will exist.

verses.sanskrit: प्रोक्षिता यत्र पशवो वधं प्राप्स्यन्ति वै मखे। यत्र पादश्चतुर्थो वै धर्मस्य न भविष्यति॥८४॥
verses.english: In the sacrifices that will be celebrated in that age, animals, after dedication with the help of sacred Mantras, will be killed. As regards virtue, again, it will lose one quarter; only three quarters thereof will remain.

verses.sanskrit: ततो वै द्वापरं नाम मिश्रः कालो भविष्यति। द्विपादहीनो धर्मश्च युगे तस्मिन् भविष्यति॥८५॥
verses.english: On the termination of the Treta, will come the mixed Yoga known by the name of Dvapara. In that cycle, virtue will lose two quarters and only two quarters thereof will remain.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तिष्येऽथ संप्राप्ते युगे कलिपुरस्कृते। एकपादस्थितो धर्मो यत्र तत्र भविष्यति॥८६॥
verses.english: Upon the termination of Dvapara, the cycle that will set in will be called Tish, and it will come with Kali walking in the van. Virtue will lose full three quarters. Only a quarter thereof will exist in all places.

verses.sanskrit: देवा देवर्षयश्चोचुस्तमेवंवादिनं गुरुम्। एकपादस्थिते धर्मे यत्र क्वचन गामिनि॥८७॥
verses.english: When the great God said these words, the gods and the celestial Rishis addressed him and said,-If only a fourth part of virtue is to exist in that age in every place, tell us, O Holy One, where shall we then go and what shall we do?

verses.sanskrit: कथं कर्तव्यमस्माभिर्भगवंस्तद्वदस्व नः। श्रीभगवानुवाच । यत्र वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च तपः सत्यं दमस्तथा॥८८॥
अहिंसाधर्मसंयुक्ताः प्रचरेयुः सुरोत्तमाः। स वो देशः सेवितव्यो मा वोऽधर्मः पदा स्पृशेत्॥८९॥
verses.english: You foremost of gods, ye should, in that age, go to such places where the Vedas and Sacrifices and Penances and Truth and selfcontrol, accompanied by duties fraught with mercy for all creatures, will still continue. Sin will never be able to affect you at all.

verses.sanskrit: व्यास उवाच । तेऽनुशिष्टा भगवता देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा। नमस्कृत्वा भगवते जग्मुर्देशान्यथेप्सितान्॥९०॥
verses.english: Vyasa said Thus commanded by the great God, the gods with all the Rishis bowed their heads to him and then proceeded to the places they desired.

verses.sanskrit: गतेषु त्रिदिवौकःसु ब्रह्मैकः पर्यवस्थितः। दिदृक्षुर्भगवन्तं तमनिरुद्धतनौ स्थितम्॥९१॥
verses.english: After the celestiats had left that place, only Brahman remained there, desirous of seeing the great Deity then living in the form of Aniruddha.

verses.sanskrit: तं देवो दर्शयामास कृत्वा हयशिरो महत्। साङ्गानावर्तयन्वेदान्कमण्डलुत्रिदण्डधृक्॥९२॥
verses.english: The foremost of gods then appeared before Brahman having assumed a form that had a huge equine head. Carrying a pitcher and the triple stick, he appeared before Brahman, reciting the Vedas with all their branches.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽश्वशिरसं दृष्ट्वा तं देवममितौजसम्। लोककर्ता प्रभुर्ब्रह्मा लोकानां हितकाम्यया॥९३॥
verses.english: Seeing the great Deity of immeasurable energy in that form with an equine head, the powerful Brahman, the Creator of all the worlds, moved by the desire of doing good to his Creation, adored that boon-giving Lord with his head down and stood before him with hands joined in respect. The great Deity embraced Brahman and then told him these words.

verses.sanskrit: मूर्ध्ना प्रणम्य वरदं तस्थौ प्राञ्जलिरग्रतः। स परिष्वज्य देवेन वचनं श्रावितस्तदा॥९४॥
श्रीभगवानुवाच । लोककार्यगती: सर्वास्त्वं चिन्तय यथाविधि। धाता त्वं सर्वभूतानां त्वं प्रभुर्जगतो गुरुः॥९५॥
verses.english: The Holy One said Do you, O Brahman, duly think of the courses of acts which creatures should follow. You are the great ordainer of all created Beings, You are the Master and the Lord of the universe. Placing this burthen on you I shall soon be free from anxiety.

verses.sanskrit: त्वय्यावेशितभारोऽहं धृतिं प्राप्स्याम्यथाञ्चसा। यदा च सुरकार्यं ते अविषह्यं भविष्यति॥९६॥
प्रादुर्भावं गमिष्यामि तदाऽऽत्मज्ञानदैशिकः। एवमुक्त्वा हयशिरास्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥९७॥
verses.english: At such time, however, when it will be difficult for you to accomplish the work of the gods, I shall then appear in incarnate forms perceiving the gravity of the emergencies.

verses.sanskrit: तेनानुशिष्टो ब्रह्मापि स्वलोकमचिराद्गतः। एवमेष महाभागः पद्मनाभः सनातनः॥९८॥
verses.english: With these words, that grand form with the equine head vanished then and there. Having received his behest, Brahman too proceeded speedily to his own region.

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञेष्वग्रहरः प्रोक्तो यज्ञधारी च नित्यदा। निवृत्तिं चास्थितो धर्मं गतिमक्षयधर्मिणाम्। प्रवृत्तिधर्मान्विदधे कृत्वा लोकस्य चित्रताम्॥९९॥
verses.english: It is for this, O Blessed One, that the eternal lotus-navelled deity became the acceptor of the first share offered in sacrifices and hence it is that He is called the eternal upholder of all Sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: युगादौ प्रबुद्धो जगद्व्युत्ससर्ज॥१००॥
verses.english: He is the beginning, He is the middle, and He is the end of all created Beings. He is their Creator and He is the actor and He is the act. Having withdrawn the universe into Himself at the end of the cycle, He enters into sleep, and awakening at the beginning of another cycle, He once more creates the universe.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मै नमध्वं देवाय निर्गुणाय महात्मने। अजाय विश्वरूपाय धाम्ने सर्वदिवौकसाम्॥१०१॥
verses.english: Do you all bow to that Illustrious One who is gifted with a high soul and who is above the : three qualities, who is Unborn, abode or refuge of all the dwellers of heaven.

verses.sanskrit: महाभूताधिपतये रुद्राणां पतये तथा। आदित्यपतये चैव वसूनां पतये तथा॥१०२॥
verses.english: Do you bow to Him who is the Supreme Lord of all creatures, who is the Lord of the Rudras, who is the Lord of the Adityas, and of the Vasus as well.

verses.sanskrit: अश्विभ्यां पतये चैव मरुतां पतये तथा। वेदयज्ञाधिपतये वेदाङ्गपतयेऽपि च॥१०३॥
verses.english: Do you bow to Him who is the Lord of the Ashvins, and the Lord of the Maruts, who is the Lord of all Sacrifices laid down in the Vedas, and the Lord of the Vedangas.

verses.sanskrit: समुद्रवासिने नित्यं हरये मुञ्जकेशिने। शान्ताय सर्वभूतानां मोक्षधर्मानुभाषिणे॥१०४॥
verses.english: Bow Him who always lives in the Ocean, and who is called Hari, and whose hair is like the blades of the Munja grass. Bow to Him who is Peace and Tranquillity, and who gives the Religion of Liberation to all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: तपसां तेजसां चैव पतये यशसामपि। वचसां पतये नित्यं सरितां पतये तथा॥१०५॥
कपर्दिने वराहाय एकशृङ्गाय धीमते। विवस्वतेऽश्वशिरसे चतुर्मूर्तिधृते सदा॥१०६॥
verses.english: Bow to Him who is called Kaparddin, who is the Geat Boar, who is the Unicorn, and who is endued with great intelligence; who is the Sun, who assumed the well-known form with the equine head; and who is always shown in a fourfold form.

verses.sanskrit: गुह्याय ज्ञानदृश्याय अक्षराय क्षराय च। एष देवः सञ्चरति सर्वत्रगतिरव्ययः॥१०७॥
verses.english: Bow to Him who is unravelled, who is capable of being apprehended by knowledge only, who is both indestructible and destructible. The supreme Deity, who is iminutable, permeates all things.

verses.sanskrit: एष चैतत्परं ब्रह्म ज्ञेयो विज्ञानचक्षुषा। एवमेतत्पुरा दृष्टं मया वै ज्ञानचक्षुषा॥१०८॥
verses.english: He is the Supreme Lord who can be known with the help of the eye of Knowledge alone. It was thus that, helped by the eye of Knowledge, I saw, in days of yore, that foremost of gods.

verses.sanskrit: कथितं तच्च वै सर्वं मया पृष्टेन तत्त्वतः। क्रियतां मद्वचः शिष्याः सेव्यतां हरिरीश्वरः। गीयतां वेदशब्दैश्च पूज्यतां च यथाविधि॥१०९॥
verses.english: Asked by you, I have told you everything in full, ye disciples, and do you act according to my words and dutifully serve the Supreme Lord called Hari. Do you sing His praises in Vedic words and adore and worship Him also according to due rites.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              इत्युक्तास्तु वयं तेन वेदव्यासेन धीमता। सर्वे शिष्या: सुतश्चास्य शुकः परमधर्मवित्॥११०॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said It was thus that the compiler of the Vedas, gifted with great intelligence, discoursed to us, accosted by us on that occasion. His son, the highly pious Shuka, and all his disciples listened to him while he delivered that discourse.

verses.sanskrit: स चास्माकमुपाध्यायः सहास्माभिर्विशांपते। चतुर्वेदोद्गताभिस्तमृग्भिः समभितुष्टुवे॥१११॥
verses.english: Our preceptor, with ourselves, O king, then worshipped the great Deity with Richs extracted from the four Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। एवं मेऽकथयद्राजन्पुरा द्वैपायनो गुरुः॥११२॥
verses.english: I have thus told you everything about what you had asked me. It was thus, O king, that our Island-born preceptor discoursed to us.

verses.sanskrit: यश्चेदं शृणुयान्नित्यं यश्चैनं परिकीर्तयेत्। नमो भगवते कृत्वा समाहितमतिर्नरः॥११३॥
verses.english: He, who, having uttered the words-'I bow to the holy Lord',-frequently listens, with rapt attention, to this discourse or reads or recites it to others, becomes gifted with intelligence and health, and possessed of beauty and strength If ill, he becomes freed from that illness; if fettered, freed from his bonds. The man who has desires gets (by this) the fruition of all his desires, and easily acquires a long life also.

verses.sanskrit: भवत्यरोगो मतिमान्बलरूपसमन्वितः। आतुरो मुच्यते रोगाद्बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात्॥११४॥
कामान्कामी लभेत्कामं दीर्घं चायुरवाप्नुयात्। ब्राह्मणः सर्ववेदी स्यात्क्षत्रियो विजयी भवेत्॥११५॥
वैश्यो विपुललाभः स्याच्छूद्रः सुखमवाप्नुयात्। अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रं कन्या चैवेप्सितं पतिम्॥११६॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, by doing this, becomes conversant with all the Vedas, and a Kshatriya becomes crowned with success. A Vaishya, by doing it, makes great profits, and a Shudra enjoys great happiness.

verses.sanskrit: लग्नगर्भा विमुच्येत गर्भिणी जनयेत्सुतम्। वन्ध्या प्रसवमाप्नोति पुत्रपौत्रसमृद्धिमत्॥११७॥
verses.english: A sonless man obtains a son. A maiden gets a desirable husband. A woman who has conceived, gives birth to a son.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेमेण गच्छेदध्वानमिदं यः पठते पथि। योऽयं कामं कामयते स तमाप्नोति च ध्रुवम्॥११८॥
verses.english: A barren woman conceives and gets many sons and grandsons. He who recites this discourse on the way succeeds in passing happily and without any obstacles along his way. In fact, one acquires whatever objects he cherishes, if one reads or recites this narrative.

verses.sanskrit: इदं महर्षेर्वचनं विनिश्चितं महात्मनः पुरुषवरस्य कीर्तितम्। समागमं चर्षिदिवौकसामिमं निशम्य भक्ताः सुसुखं लभन्ते॥११९॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of the great Rishi, fraught with certainty of conclusion, and containing a recital of the attributes of that great one who is the foremost of all beings, hearing this narrative of the great assembly of Rishis and other dwellers of heaven,-men who are devoted to the Supreme Deity derive great happiness.
